column1: # What to record, and which ledger row each recording pays off.
#   group     a key from `unrecorded` in internal/lint/evidence_test.go
#   cassette  the file to write, relative to the repository root
#   command   the jr invocation that produces it, or `!<reason>` for a row no
#             single invocation can produce. Shell quoting applies inside this
#             field, because a JQL string is one argument and word-splitting a
#             manifest is how it stops being one.
# internal/lint/dcmanifest_test.go reads this file and requires every
# outstanding Data Center row to appear here, so the checklist is read by the
# build rather than by whoever remembers to open the README.
# The commands assume the seed: project ENG, board 1, users ada and grace.

column3: !TestContractAgainstBothDeployments plays exactly four interactions — serverInfo, myself, a 404 issue GET, and a POST that must 400 on summary — and no single jr invocation produces that set. Recording it needs the four merged, or the test taught to drive a cassette recorded by a command.

column1: # The two halves of what a comma in a repeatable filter costs. Jira validates a
# status name and refuses one it does not know, so `--status Done,Closed` is one
# status with a comma in it and fails loudly. It does not validate a label, so
# `--label a,b` is one label with a comma in it and comes back complete, empty,
# and exit 0. Recorded because the argument for leaving both unsplit rests on
# what the server does, and nothing had asked it.

column3: jql validate --jql 'project = ENG ORDER BY key DESC'

column1: # The refusal is version-specific and credential-specific: an 11.x instance,
# and a basic credential, which no seeded profile holds because the seeded one
# holds a token that works. record-auth-refusal.sh makes both.

column3: !recorded by scripts/dc/record-auth-refusal.sh, which needs JIRA_VERSION=11.3.5 and stores a basic credential with --no-verify

column1: # The write verbs are a sequence, not a set: each needs the instance in the
# state the one before it left, and two of them need an id that only the step
# before can supply. scripts/dc/record-writes.sh is the unit of reproduction,
# and the command each row would have carried is written out beside it.

column3: !scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue create --project ENG --type Task --summary 'Recorded write path' --description ...
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue edit <subject> --summary 'Recorded write path, edited'
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue assign <subject> grace
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue comment add <subject> 'Recorded by the fixture rig'
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue comment delete <subject> <the id the add returned> --yes
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue worklog add <subject> 1h
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue worklog delete <subject> <the id the add returned> --yes
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue link add <subject> 'relates to' ENG-2
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue move <subject> <the first transition that changes the status>
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue clone <subject> --summary 'Recorded write path, cloned'
!scripts/dc/record-writes.sh, which runs: jr issue delete <the clone> --yes

column1: # The last two of the three bugs this project cites live behind these: the
# createmeta route removed in Jira 9.0, and the transitions this tool must never
# cache. Both are read through internal/site, so the recordings sit with the
# code rather than with the command.
# Two of the failure fixtures can be recorded and three cannot: a healthy
# server does not answer 503 on request, and a cassette holding an interaction
# that must never be played is not a recording of anything. Each of those three
# says so in its own note field.

column3: !scripts/dc/record-refusals.sh, which runs two identical `issue create --project ENG --type Bug --summary "a summary"` and concatenates them
!scripts/dc/record-refusals.sh, which creates a Task, gives it a Sub-task, and runs: jr issue delete <parent> --yes
